M3 requires each surrogate to run inside the coupling loop, to be differentiable there, and
to have its cost measured. The structured electron-cyclotron (EC) surrogate
([entry 38](38-structured-ec-surrogate.qmd)) and the ITER pedestal network
([entry 36](36-ec-and-pedestal-contracts.qmd)) existed only as standalone models. The
[Primer](../primer.qmd) explains sources and the pedestal; terms are in the
[Glossary](../glossary.qmd).

**EC.** TORAX's EC source already returns both a heating profile and a driven-current
profile, so the surrogate is registered as a new model of that source rather than as a new
channel. At each step it reads the electron temperature, density and effective charge from
TORAX's state, evaluates the ensemble, and rebuilds the two profiles on TORAX's own cells so
that their integrals equal the predicted totals. A guard decides for the whole profile: if the
inputs leave the training box or the ensemble members disagree too much, TORAX's Gaussian EC
model with parameters fitted to the GENRAY labels is used instead. A first version rebuilt the
model function on every run, so TORAX recompiled each time; it is now cached.

**Pedestal.** The network is registered as a TORAX pedestal model whose prescribed values are
the fallback. Its ten inputs come from TORAX's geometry and profiles, including the normalised
beta computed by TORAX. One input needed a convention: EPED takes the ion mass number (2.5 for
deuterium-tritium), while TORAX holds the mass in atomic units, slightly above the network's
training range. With the mass number, the network sets the pedestal on every state.

**Checks.** On the ITER hybrid scenario, with part of the scenario's generic heating moved to EC at the
same total power, both models run in TORAX's compiled step with the Newton solver, close the discrete
energy and particle balance, and have derivatives through the solver that agree with finite
differences ([runs under jit for both launchers with the surrogate serving the source; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7]{.claim}[C-171](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-171){.cid .st-tested}; [runs under jit with EPEDNN setting the pedestal; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7]{.claim}[C-173](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-173){.cid .st-tested}). These checks compare the coupled code
with itself under perturbation; they do not test the physics of either reference.

| quantity | result |
|---|---|
| EC over the full trajectory | [surrogate serves 29 of 30 states (upper launcher) and 16 of 27 (equatorial; core T_e leaves the training range); run time 1.6-1.7 times the analytic source; one call 39 microseconds against 85 s for GENRAY]{.claim}[C-172](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-172){.cid .st-measured} |
| pedestal over the full trajectory | [EPEDNN sets the pedestal on 48 of 48 states: T_ped 2.62-2.69 keV, top 0.90-0.92; final stored thermal energy 220 MJ against 303 MJ, beta_N 1.57 against 2.16; about 1.5 times the prescribed model per step]{.claim}[C-174](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-174){.cid .st-measured} |

With central EC deposition the core temperature rises past the largest value in the EC
training data, and the guard hands over to the fallback for the rest of that run. The upper
launcher deposits off-axis and the surrogate serves almost every state. The network's pedestal
is lower than the scenario's prescribed one, and stored energy and normalised beta fall with
it; normalised beta is also an input to the network, so the loop settles on a consistent
value.

All four M3 surrogates (transport per machine, EC, ITER pedestal) now run inside TORAX. The
remaining question for M3 is in the next entry.
